newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two kidnapped Russian reporters freed in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Two kidnapped Russian reporters freed in Chechnya.

text.p: Authorities in Russia's breakaway region of Chechnya said on Tuesday that they had secured the release of two Russian journalists kidnapped in March by bandits.

Chechen Interior Minister Kazbek Makhashev told Reuters that Olga Bagautdinova and Alexander Utrobin, who work for a local newspaper in the Urals region, had been freed by the secessionist region's security forces.
He said the two reporters were well but gave no further details.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted Makhashev as saying he had hopes that four other missing Russian journalists would soon be released.
An Italian photographer was freed by kidnappers last month.

Kidnappings, usually for ransom, have become a common occurrence in Chechnya, where nearly all men are armed and which was devastated during a 21-month conflict between Russian troops and pro-independence guerrillas that ended last August.

Russian and Chechen officials are now conducting difficult talks aimed at mapping out a new relationship between Moscow and the mainly Moslem North Caucasus territory. President Aslan Maskhadov is expected to visit Moscow later this month.

Tass said Makhashev would speak by telephone later on Tuesday with Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov on plans to set up a joint Russian-Chechen commission to investigate a recent spate of bombings in southern Russia.

Four people died and many more were injured in two bomb explosions in the towns of Armavir and Pyatigorsk last month. Radical Chechen guerrilla commander Salman Raduyev has claimed responsibility for the attacks, which he said were a result of Moscow's refusal to recognise Chechen independence.
On Monday Chechen officials said they had issued a warrant for Raduyev's arrest.

Kulikov told Ekho Moskvy radio that Raduyev would be arrested "at the first opportunity". Interior Ministry troops backed up by aircraft and tanks allowed Raduyev to slip through their lines when they had him surrounded with over 100 hostages at the village of Pervomaiskoye in January 1996.
